protocol: read-only: reuse frozen 5-truck test split and saved M1.2 artifacts; corruption applied to copies of the final model-input feature matrices after feature construction and before preprocessing; no training/refitting/tuning
analysis_frame: synthetic corruption applied to copies of the model-input feature matrices; results are descriptive pipeline validation, NOT observed real-world sensor-failure data

full_operational.basis: validation MAE (M1.2) — test data not used

telematics_only.basis: validation MAE (M1.2) — test data not used

training_statistics_provenance.description: Gaussian-noise sigma and spike reference statistics (median, std) are derived exclusively from the training split of the frozen split manifest; never from validation or test data. Severity multipliers, bias magnitudes and clipping bounds are predefined documented constants.

random_stream.description: Each affected column uses an independent RNG seeded deterministically from the scenario seed plus a stable hash of the column name; shared columns receive identical corruption across feature sets (same scenario, same row indices).

combined_scenario.note: The combined missingness+noise scenario uses an independent realization from the standalone 20% missingness and 0.25-noise scenarios (separate seeds), not a superset of them.

limitations: Synthetic telemetry: these are pipeline-corruption experiments on synthetic data, not observed real-world sensor-failure validation. They characterize model sensitivity to the injected corruptions only.
Only five test trucks: all per-truck breakdowns are descriptive and unstable; not population estimates.
Corruption is restricted to numeric model-input features; categorical vehicle_class and binary ignition_status are kept unchanged. Real-world sensor failures may also affect other signal classes.
No feature columns are removed; complete sensor failure is simulated with all-NaN values while preserving the model's expected schema.

Prediction failures (aborted, NaN, +inf or -inf predictions) are counted and reported as a failure rate; metrics are computed on the surviving finite rows and should always be read alongside the failure rate.
The clipping bounds are documented physical limits; they are already satisfied by most data, so the clipping scenario primarily measures the effect of the bound enforcement itself.
MAE degradation is reported against each feature set's own clean baseline; cross-feature-set ratios are not directly comparable because baselines differ.
